section.content: The invention provides a semiconductor device and a semiconductor integrated circuit, which comprises an element isolation region (14), a convex semiconductor region (11), and gate electrodes formed on both side surfaces and the upper surface of a part of the convex semiconductor region, and a plurality of first gate electrodes (12A) formed between a pair of opposite ends of the element isolation region, the first gate electrodes being formed between the plurality of first gate electrodes on the same layer as the plurality of first gate electrodes, at least one second gate electrode (12B) for applying a voltage to turn off the transistor, and a source region and a drain region formed in the semiconductor region on both sides of the first gate electrode and the second gate electrode, a transistor having a second gate electrode to which a voltage to be turned off is applied is arranged between transistors having first gate electrodes, so that heat generation in the transistor is reduced without lowering the saturation current of the transistor.

本发明提供一种半导体装置以及半导体集成电路，具有元件分离区域(14)、凸状的半导体区域(11)、形成于凸状的半导体区域的一部分的两个侧面以及上表面的栅电极，且是形成在元件分离区域的对置的一对端部之间的多个第一栅电极(12A)、在与多个第一栅电极相同的层形成在多个第一栅电极之间，并施加将晶体管设为截止状态的电压的至少一个第二栅电极(12B)以及源极区域和漏极区域，形成于第一栅电极和第二栅电极的两侧的凸状的半导体区域，在具有第一栅电极的晶体管之间，配置具有施加成为截止状态的电压的第二栅电极的晶体管，从而不降低晶体管的饱和电流而减少晶体管中的发热。

Semiconductor device and semiconductor integrated circuitTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a semiconductor device and a semiconductor integrated circuit.

Background

A Field Effect Transistor (FinFET) has a structure in which a gate insulating film and a gate electrode are formed on both side surfaces and an upper surface of a part of a convex (Fin-shaped) semiconductor region formed on a substrate and extending in one direction, and a Fin-shaped source region and a Fin-shaped drain region are formed in the convex semiconductor region on both sides of the gate electrode (see, for example, patent document 1). Finfets in their structure, since heat is easily left, need a way to reduce heat generation by layout.

Fig. 8 is a diagram showing an example of a FinFET having a multi-finger structure in which a plurality of gate electrodes are formed in a comb-tooth shape (finger shape). In fig. 8, 101 denotes a semiconductor region formed on a substrate and having a convex shape (rib shape) extending in one direction.

A part of the convex semiconductor region 101 is formed so that a gate electrode 102 whose both side surfaces and upper surface are covered with a gate insulating film is intersected with the convex semiconductor region 101, and a source region and a drain region are formed in the convex semiconductor region 101 on both sides of the gate electrode 102. The plurality of gate electrodes 102 are made of, for example, polysilicon, and are connected to the metal wiring 103 via a via hole.

In fig. 8, 104 denotes an element Isolation insulating film (STI) for isolating a region where a transistor is to be formed, and 105 denotes a dummy gate electrode, which is disposed between the gate electrode 102 and the STI104 and is formed in the same layer as the gate electrode 102. The dummy gate electrode 105 is also made of, for example, polysilicon.

Finfets with a multi-finger structure are affected by heat generation of adjacent transistors, and as shown in fig. 9, the larger the number of fingers, the more easily heat. In other words, if the FinFET has a multi-finger structure as shown in fig. 8, heat is more likely to be generated than in the case where the number of fingers is 1.

As one method of suppressing heat generation of the FinFET, as shown in fig. 10, a method of suppressing heat generation by reducing the influence of heat generation from adjacent transistors by setting the number of fingers to 1 or the like is considered. Fig. 10 is a diagram showing an example of a FinFET structure in which the number of fingers is 1, and the same components as those shown in fig. 8 are denoted by the same reference numerals.

However, as shown in fig. 10, in the FinFET having the number of fingers set to 1, the distance x between the STIs 104 disposed on both sides of the gate electrode 102 becomes short. When the distance x between the STIs 104 is short, the saturation current Ion of the transistor shown in fig. 11 decreases due to STI stress (stress due to the STIs 104). Therefore, in order to obtain the same saturation current Ion as that of the FinFET having the multi-finger structure shown in fig. 8, for example, the number of transistors needs to be increased, which results in increased power consumption and increased area.

Patent document 1 Japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2015-220420

Disclosure of Invention

The present invention aims to provide a FinFET type semiconductor device capable of reducing heat generation in a transistor without reducing saturation current of the transistor.

One embodiment of a semiconductor device includes: an element separating region; a convex semiconductor region; a plurality of first gate electrodes formed on both side surfaces and an upper surface of a part of the convex semiconductor region, and formed between a pair of opposite end portions of the element isolation region to constitute a plurality of transistors; and a second gate electrode which is formed between the plurality of first gate electrodes on the same layer as the plurality of first gate electrodes and applies a voltage for turning off the transistor.

In the disclosed semiconductor device, a transistor having a second gate electrode to which a voltage to be turned off is applied is arranged between transistors having first gate electrodes, whereby heat generation in the transistors can be reduced without reducing the saturation current of the transistors.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described with reference to the drawings.

Fig. 1 is a diagram showing an example of a structure of a Field Effect Transistor (FinFET) having a Fin-shaped structure as a semiconductor device according to an embodiment of the present invention. Fig. 2A is a schematic sectional view taken along line I-I of fig. 1, fig. 2B is a schematic sectional view taken along line II-II of fig. 1, and fig. 2C is a schematic sectional view taken along line III-III of fig. 1.

The FinFET in the present embodiment has a semiconductor region 11 of a convex shape (rib shape) extending in one direction formed on a substrate 17. A gate insulating film, not shown, is formed on both side surfaces and an upper surface of a part of the convex semiconductor region 11. Gate electrodes 12A and 12B covered with a gate insulating film are formed on both side surfaces and an upper surface of a part of the convex semiconductor region 11. In the covering portion of the gate insulating film of the convex semiconductor region 11, in other words, the convex semiconductor region 11 on both sides of the gate electrodes 12A and 12B, an active region and a drain region are formed.

The gate electrodes 12A and 12B are formed in the same layer between a pair of opposite ends of the element isolation region, and are made of, for example, polysilicon. The gate electrodes 12A are connected to metal wirings 13A to which signals are input via holes 16A, respectively. The gate electrodes 12B are connected to metal wirings 13B to which the same voltage as the back gate is applied via holes 16B, respectively. The source region and the drain region formed in the convex semiconductor region 11 are connected to a source electrode and a drain electrode, respectively, via contact electrodes, not shown.

In addition, an element Isolation insulating film (STI) 14 for isolating a region where a transistor is formed on the substrate 17. Between the STI14 and the gate electrode 12A or 12B, a dummy gate electrode 15 made of, for example, polysilicon is formed in the same layer as the gate electrodes 12A and 12B. The semiconductor device shown in fig. 1, 2A, 2B, and 2C can be formed by a known manufacturing method, for example, at least a part of the manufacturing method described in patent document 1.

As described above, the FinFET of the present embodiment has a multi-finger structure in which a plurality of gate electrodes 12A to which signals are applied are formed in a comb-tooth shape (finger shape) between a pair of opposing end portions of an element isolation region where STI14 is arranged, and a gate electrode 12B to which the same voltage as that of a back gate is applied is provided between the gate electrodes 12A to which signals are applied. That is, a transistor MB that limits the potential of the gate electrode 12B to an off state is disposed between the transistors MA driven by a signal.

This can suppress heat generation in the FinFET. Further, the distance between the STI14 formed on both sides of the gate electrode is sufficiently long, and the STI stress can be relaxed to maintain the saturation current Ion.

In the above example, the gate electrode 12A to which a signal is input and the gate electrode 12B to which the same voltage as the back gate is applied are alternately provided. That is, one transistor which limits the potential of the gate electrode to an off state is provided between the transistors driven in accordance with the signal. However, the present invention is not limited thereto.

The number of gate electrodes 12B to which the same voltage as the back gate is applied, which are provided between the gate electrodes 12A to which a signal is input, is arbitrary, and for example, 2 gate electrodes 12B to which the same voltage as the back gate is applied may be provided between the gate electrodes 12A to which a signal is input, as shown in fig. 3. That is, 2 transistors which limit the potential of the gate electrode to an off state may be provided between the transistors which are driven in accordance with the signal.

For example, as shown in fig. 4, 2 gate electrodes 12A to which signals are input may be arranged adjacent to each other, and 1 gate electrode 12B to which the same voltage as that of the back gate is applied may be provided therebetween. That is, 2 transistors driven in accordance with a signal may be adjacent to each other, and 1 transistor which limits the potential of the gate electrode to an off state may be provided therebetween.

Further, for example, as shown in fig. 5, 2 gate electrodes 12A to which signals are input may be arranged adjacent to each other, and 2 gate electrodes 12B to which the same voltage as the back gate is applied may be provided therebetween. That is, 2 transistors driven in accordance with a signal may be adjacent to each other, and 2 transistors which limit the potential of the gate electrode to an off state may be provided therebetween. Further, since heat generation increases when the number of transistors driven by a signal is increased in adjacent arrangement, it is preferable to arrange 1 or 2 transistors driven by a signal in adjacent arrangement.

Next, a semiconductor integrated circuit to which the FinFET in this embodiment is applied will be described. Fig. 6A is a circuit diagram showing an example of a configuration of a Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO) as an application example of the FinFET in the present embodiment. The voltage controlled oscillation circuit has P-channel transistors M11, M13, N-channel transistors M12, M14, an inductor L11, a capacitor C11, and a voltage controlled variable capacitor C12.

The P-channel transistor M11 has a source connected to a signal line for supplying the power supply voltage VDD, and a drain connected to the drain of the N-channel transistor M12. The source of the N-channel transistor M12 is connected to a signal line that supplies a reference voltage (e.g., ground GND).

Similarly, the P-channel transistor M13 has a source connected to a signal line for supplying the power supply voltage VDD, and a drain connected to the drain of the N-channel transistor M14. The source of the N-channel transistor M14 is connected to a signal line for supplying a reference voltage.

In addition, the gate of the P-channel transistor M11 and the gate of the N-channel transistor M12 are connected to the interconnection point of the drain of the P-channel transistor M13 and the drain of the N-channel transistor M14. The gate of the P-channel transistor M13 and the gate of the N-channel transistor M14 are connected to the interconnection of the drain of the P-channel transistor M11 and the drain of the N-channel transistor M12. That is, the first inverter composed of transistors M11, M12 and the second inverter composed of transistors M13, M14 are cross-coupled.

An inductor L11, a capacitor C11, and a variable capacitor C12 are connected in parallel between a connection point of the drains of the transistors M11, M12 and a connection point of the drains of the transistors M13, M14.

The oscillation frequency f of the oscillation circuit shown in fig. 6A is determined by an inductor L11, a capacitor C11, and a variable capacitor C12, and is represented by f ═ 1/(2 √ (L11(C11+ C12))). The inductor L11 and the capacitor C11 are reduced in order to realize a high-frequency oscillation frequency, but since it is difficult to oscillate if the inductor L11 is excessively reduced, the capacitor C11 is generally reduced.

As a component of the capacitor C11, a parasitic load of a wiring and a cross-coupled transistor load are dominant. Since the oscillation signal is a sine wave, the transistors M11 to M14 tend to be in an on state for a relatively long period of time and tend to generate heat easily. Here, for example, if heat generation is to be suppressed as shown in fig. 10, the load due to the wiring increases and the saturation current Ion of the transistor decreases, so that the number of transistors needs to be increased. As a result, the capacitance C11 increases, and it becomes difficult to achieve a desired oscillation frequency.

By applying the FinFET of this embodiment to the transistors M11 to M14, heat generation can be suppressed without lowering the saturation current Ion of the transistors, and a signal of a desired oscillation frequency can be output while suppressing an increase in the capacitance C11 due to a wiring load.

For example, by configuring the P-channel transistors M11 and M13 as shown in fig. 6B and configuring the N-channel transistors M12 and M14 as shown in fig. 6C, heat generation can be suppressed without lowering the saturation current Ion of the transistors. Fig. 6B and 6C are diagrams showing a configuration example of the P-channel transistors M11 and M13 and the N-channel transistors M12 and M14 shown in fig. 6A, and the same reference numerals are given to the same components as those shown in fig. 1.

The FinFET shown in fig. 6B has a source region of a transistor having the gate electrode 12A as a gate electrode formed in the semiconductor region 11 between the gate electrode 12A and the gate electrode 12B (or the dummy gate electrode 15), and a drain region formed in the semiconductor region 11 between adjacent gate electrodes 12A. A source region of the transistor having the gate electrode 12A as a gate electrode is connected to a source electrode for supplying the power supply voltage VDD via a contact electrode not shown, and a drain region is connected to a drain electrode via a contact electrode not shown.

In the FinFET shown in fig. 6C, the source region of the transistor having the gate electrode 12A as the gate electrode is formed in the semiconductor region 11 between the gate electrode 12A and the gate electrode 12B (or the dummy gate electrode 15), and the drain region is formed in the semiconductor region 11 between the adjacent gate electrodes 12A. A source region of the transistor having the gate electrode 12A as a gate electrode is connected to a source electrode to which a reference voltage (for example, ground GND) is supplied via a contact electrode (not shown), and a drain region is connected to a drain electrode via a contact electrode (not shown).

Fig. 7A is a circuit diagram showing an example of the configuration of a bias circuit as an application example of the FinFET in the present embodiment. The bias circuit shown in fig. 7A is a circuit in which P-channel transistors M21 and M22 are current-mirror-connected and a current 2 times the current I1 flows as the current I2.

For example, by configuring the P-channel transistors M21 and M22 as shown in fig. 7B, heat generation can be suppressed without lowering the saturation current Ion of the transistors. Fig. 7B is a diagram showing an example of the configuration of the P-channel transistors M21 and M22 shown in fig. 7A, and the same components as those shown in fig. 1 are denoted by the same reference numerals. By using a transistor having 1 group of 2 adjacent gate electrodes 12A as the P-channel transistor M21 and using a transistor having 2 groups of 2 adjacent gate electrodes 12A as the P-channel transistor M22, a current 2 times as large as the current I1 flowing in the transistor M21 can flow as the current I2.

The above embodiments are merely specific examples for carrying out the present invention, and the technical scope of the present invention is not to be construed in a limiting manner. That is, the present invention can be implemented in various forms without departing from the technical idea or main features thereof.

According to the present invention, in the FinFET, the transistor having the gate electrode to which the voltage to be turned off is applied is arranged between the transistors having the gate electrodes to which the signals are applied, whereby heat generation in the transistors can be reduced without reducing the saturation current of the transistors.
